t: Ammer. An allod formed on the site of the battle (and death) of Sarn and the Architect. It is distinctive in that its shape resembles a statue. The climate on the allod is temperate. It is home to the Aoidoi race. In the Astral near the allod live demons of the latest generation, as well as demons neutral towards the living. Near the allod lies an islet with an observatory — a complex for travelling into the past and the future.

t: Avilon. The allod belongs to the Historians' faction and is held by their leader, the Great Mage Zayan. The climate is temperate. After the start of the Allods Online storyline it is attacked by demons and Sarn's cultists, supported by a huge flying galleon-ship built by the Great Mage Gorluxor. By the end of the storyline the attack has been repelled, and the ship captured; the Historians now use it.

t: Dragon Ring. In fact it is an archipelago of small allods. The climate is tropical. It belongs, as you might easily guess, to the descendants of the last surviving dragons. Its native population is lizards and the draconids stamped out of them. At first it was thought to be held by a dragoness named Soliskar, but she later flew off on her own business while the archipelago remained. So this archipelago apparently exists either thanks to meteorite iron or thanks to some artefact.

t: Ferris. At the start of the Allods Online storyline the allod is neutral; by its end it is occupied by the League and the Empire. Its native population is the savage Tungars. Before the storyline began, the allod housed an imperial research base, "Project Gates", which studied the construction of a portal to other worlds and one of the captured inhabitants of such another world (and, on top of that, the modification of living beings, the creation of mechanoids and the study of cloning). But the otherworlder proved unexpectedly powerful and managed to turn almost all the inhabitants of the base into monsters, who slaughtered the rest. Only a cultist of Tep who had infiltrated the project's leadership survived, and at the end of the Allods Online storyline he is still running around somewhere in the basements of the laboratory complex. Cloning was first invented right here, though the technology did not reach the Empire at the time. How Sarn's cultists managed to obtain it is unclear.

t: Gipat. Once one of the last dwelling places of the June race. At the start of the Allods Online storyline it had split into many shards. The largest shards exist by the will of Nihaz (one is called the Gipat Shard, the other the Isle of Revelation — more on it below) and serve to reveal the truth about Sarnaut and Sarn. The climate on the Gipat Shard is temperate. A small islet near the allod is used by Nihaz's servants to house the Whirlpool of Time, a device for travelling into the past (and possibly into the future). Among the smaller shards of Gipat, Allods Online also features the Wandering Island, the Twilight Isle, the Dead City and the Frozen Peak.

t: Holy Land. The allegiance of the allod is disputed: not only do the League and the Empire fight over it, but part of the allod has also been seized by the goblin mafia. Its native population is human. Every possible kind of climate is represented. It is distinguished by a pyramid of Tep in which dwells the Spark of Tensess (the very one who granted everyone immortality). Because of this, some artefacts of the Zem people (that is, the ancient ones, from before Tep killed everyone) became saturated with holy magic and acquired unexpected but extremely powerful properties. Then Sarn's cultists and their demons meddled, and the artefacts' properties became more unexpected still.

t:
Igsh is a metropolitan allod geographically divided into two parts - steppe and desert.  The desert is the bottom of an ancient sea which was exposed after the world split into allods. Steppe is the part of those lands that occupied the entire eastern outskirts of Yul.

Their flora and fauna are quite typical for these territories. However, it should be noted that due to the increasing urbanization, they are significantly degrading. Igsh rhinos and unicorns used for commercial hunting are becoming rare species.

Another threat to the animals is the Necro-Incubator. Its creations wander around the steppes and destroy everything they can reach.

The only prosperous community on Igsh are termites which have grown in numbers in recent years. This tendency is only a part of the general changes of this kind that occur throughout Sarnaut. It appears to be connected with the influence of the astral plane.
Igsh. The main allod of the Empire. The climate is predominantly desert. Its native population is Xadaganians and Zem. The allod is home to the capital of the Empire, Nezebgrad.

t: Once the elves had a single kingdom — Irene. After the fall of the June nothing could compare with the might of this kingdom, in which even the lowliest vagabond wielded magic. Striving to become stronger still, the elite of this elven kingdom delved ever deeper into hitherto unexplored realms of magic. The elves' attention was drawn to the mysterious magic of the June — blood magic. Using the rituals of blood magic, some elves became vampires and were doomed to an eternal thirst that could only be quenched with the blood of others. These events became known as the "Blood Feast". The problem was eventually brought under control, but it did not pass without a trace for Irene: trust among the elves was shattered. Many of them left the kingdom, settling in various hidden corners of Yul. A little later the elves began to form Houses — families, each of which lived by its own laws and rules.

The Gibberlings called their small continent Isa — "the island" — and grew used to thinking of the sea as their native element and of a ship as their home.

There was a place on Isa sacred to all Gibberlings: a place where the realms of ice and fire meet, where the Great Tree grows, from whose branches, legend has it, the first Gibberlings, As and Emla, were made.

Along with the Gibberlings, Isa was also home to the Praiden and to tribes of wild orcs.

This continent was lost in the Cataclysm, shattering into pieces. One of those shards is Howlem.
f: Long believed lost (in fact it had been hidden by magic). In the 14.0 storyline, while searching for a way to save the Great Trees that had begun dying all across Sarnaut, we reach it from Howlem.

t: Kania. The main allod of the League. Its native population is Kanians and, strangely enough, Zem — though the Zem on Kania could not come back to life properly and are mindless undead. The allod is home to the capital of the League, Novograd, as well as the cursed castle of the Valir dynasty, one of Tep's pyramids and the Great Tree. The climate is temperate in places and tundra in others.

t: Sogot. The main allod of the demonologists. Sarn originally used it for experiments on demons, so its climate is impossible to determine: the whole allod is covered with an unbroken layer of demon bones that have piled up there almost since the Cataclysm. For a time it was captured by the Demon Hunters, who even managed to build one of their citadels on it. But then the demons took the allod back.

t:
Suslanger is a unique case. It's all about the recent events.

Without a doubt, we are dealing with something unknown.

This "Ambrosia", as someone called it, is something incredible. We are dealing with a form of life that encompasses both animal and plant life. Moreover, it seems that the Ambrosia exists in a form that was not previously considered living - minerals.

We have never had anything like it. Neither the Blight I studied nor the modifiers come anywhere close. I am not inclined to pathos, but I am willing to swear that this is the real concentrated essence of Life itself. It would be nice to understand where it came from...

Scorching Suslanger will especially delight lovers of necromancy — these lands are literally teeming with the spawn of sinister magic. Nor will those who enjoy exploring dungeons inhabited by the most incredible creatures be disappointed.

Suslanger is a sun-scorched desert. This small island belongs to the Xadagan Empire. Geographically it is divided into two halves: a lowland, comparatively fertile, and an upland, which is desert. The upland is split in two by a huge Canyon carved by a river that flows into a small lake. There is little land on Suslanger fit for living and farming. The river and the lake are the only large sources of water. To extend the cultivated land at least a little, people have to build irrigation canals and dams. Several settlements lie around the lake. There are almost no settlements in the desert, where a few orc tribes still live — strong and skilled enough to survive alongside the Xadaganians, and clever enough not to provoke them into a major war.

Power in Xadagan is harsh and merciless. A numerous guard punishes the slightest breach of the emperor's decrees, while spies and informers report on every suspicious person. Suslanger is of little economic importance to Xadagan, but it is home to a military academy whose graduates hold prominent posts in the imperial army.

Suslanger. It belongs to the Empire. The climate is desert. Its native inhabitants are Xadaganians. Construction of the "Gates-3" facility has begun. The island has opened to free visits and been declared a peaceful zone; now you can see Gibberlings relaxing under the hot wind and the blazing sun, Kanian recruits in the ranks of the local pioneers, while Zem scholars freely exchange their knowledge with elven engineers.

t:
The allod of Umoir, the first to be surrounded by a magical protection against the Astral, is the largest island-shard of Sarnaut. The allod abounds in small villages, forests, lakes and all kinds of wildlife, and at its very centre stands the tower of the Great Mage Skrakan.

Geography:
The climate of the allod is warm and pleasant; everything grows here, and the lush groves are ample proof of it. High mountains can be found in the north, but on the whole plains prevail. The allod is very large, so several forests spread across it at once, the largest of which is Rotwood.

Inhabitants
Most of the allod's population are humans, living in many villages and in the large city of Plagot. The city boasts a rich tavern where travellers, dashing mercenaries and other folk gather, a school of magic and trading shops. Formally the allod of Umoir belongs to no state, but thanks to its mysterious sealing both empires took a keen interest in it, and Skrakan's leaning towards the Kanians and his firm friendship with Tensess are common knowledge.

Umoir. Formally it belongs to the League, in fact it is neutral. It is under the rule of the Great Mage Catherina. The climate is mostly temperate, desert in places. Its native population is Kanians and elves — though by the start of the storyline the elves had been driven off to a small neighbouring allod. Umoir was formerly ruled by the Great Mage Skrakan. It is marked by an epidemic of a disease called the Plague, which transforms every living thing. It later turned out that Sarn was behind the spread of the disease, but by the end of the storyline the disease has not gone anywhere — it has simply stopped spreading. The allod is notable for the ruins of a city from the first game in the series ("Allods: Rage of Mages"), Plagot, and for the barrow where a demon from that same first game of the universe is buried. On top of that, a large community of pagans lives on the allod, worshipping, among other gods, the daughter of the God of Darkness — Klavdia.

It is considered the largest allod of Sarnaut.
f: Catherina (Great Mage) and her apprentice Zarida Zharova

Ark was originally a small principality in the far south-west of Kania. Nezeb's conquest, when he unleashed the hordes of Ugr on the southern borders, passed it by, but at the same time cut it off from the main body of Kanian lands. Erast himself considered himself independent, yet showed Nezeb various signs of respect — he was, after all, the nearest neighbour. The Xadagan emperor did not dare touch Ark either: the profits from trade were considerable, and simply seizing such a scrap of land would bring no benefit. If you were to choose a place to live as you please, Ark could well be it. Neither Kania nor Xadagan collects taxes or recruits troops there; live and let live. Besides, there were no threats on Ark at all… except perhaps a few trolls and kobolds in the mountain caves, but they did not risk coming down into the valley. And the people of Ark, of course, are cheerful. Kanians and Xadaganians have mixed here so long ago that you cannot tell one from the other. Elves lived in these lost lands too — the House de Ark.

Forox is one of the main Kanian allods, alongside Kania and Umoir.

This land is the birthplace of the Great Mage Aidenus, who held the allod together against the destructive force of the Astral during the Cataclysm. After Aidenus began holding Kania, the Great Mage Bogsha — evidently a disciple of Aidenus — settled in Rakhl-Forox, the Tower of the Great Mage of Forox. It was thanks to Bogsha's efforts that the people elected Ivan the Ascetic, a priest of the Church of Light, as Governor. Under him the Church of Light gained enormous power on Forox, and the allod itself effectively became the Church's domain. Unfortunately, Bogsha went missing in the Misty Valley of Forox, after which the allod came to be held by his disciple, Tritogor. From the words of Tritogor's own disciple, Wienna, we learn that "something dark took hold of Tritogor's mind", and under his rule Forox was nearly emptied of people.

The Free City, located on the allod of Tortuga, was an early concept (of Allods Online) conceived as a centre of piracy. Very early work on it was found in the game files; the idea was eventually abandoned.

The city was laid out in an arc, forming the shape of a gulf or bay. In the middle was a pier, behind it buildings, and higher still a Central building with a balloon. A Lighthouse presumably stood at the centre of the bay. The city had three tiers.

Gelida is the elven allod of the Great House de Blizare: a very frosty place, but thanks to elven potions the elves know no hardship. It is always warm in their palaces, even when a snowstorm rages outside the window. Besides the elves, tribes of Forestfolk live on Gelida. The elves have taught them a great deal, and in return received their boundless loyalty and devotion. It is also the abode of the lesser House de Ruse, which provides food for the elves from the snowy forests, rich in game, and the lakes full of fish.

[Map missing]

Grok is a vast steppe; small forests and mountains are found only at the edges of the island.

Originally the allod belonged to the elves of the House de Vevre (in the days before the League existed), who had several small towns here. The local steppes are not very fertile: there are few rivers and cold winds often blew, so grain did not grow well. Magic helped the elves in this, and besides magic they found another solution — raising all kinds of livestock.

Besides the elves, orcs lived in the steppes a little beyond the centre of the allod. The House de Vevre would of course have liked to be rid of the orcs — but how do you chase them across the steppe?

Claude de Vevre, the Great Mage of Grok, once tried to teach the orc Rodogor magic (for it was here that Lorzub the Fierce, the Legendary Orc, was born), making him his disciple, but these efforts bore no fruit: the orcs proved incapable of magic. The angered Rodogor turned to Nezeb, the Great Mage of Igsh and leader of Xadagan.

In the year 707 of the New Era, the orcs and the Xadaganians captured Grok, killing Claude de Vevre, the Great Mage of the allod. Nezeb kept the promise he had made to Rodogor, and a Xadagan Great Mage began holding the allod.

t:
Istinsk is one of the recently settled allods. It is a typical allod with steady frosty weather, rich in meteorite and other ore deposits.

Despite the harsh conditions, it has a fairly diverse fauna consisting of typical inhabitants of coniferous forests. Additionally, there is a lake full of commercial fish species in the center of the allod.

However, the mining of ore in the mountains and quarries poses a certain danger to the biodiversity of this allod.

t:
Izune is an Orc allod which became part of the Empire after the annexation of the Orcs. A typical example of the steppe allods formed when the eastern part of the continent split apart.  The only difference is the old volcano in the very center of the allod where a dragon once dwelled.

The approaches to the volcano are overgrown with forest, but the rest are bare steppes. Izune is quite poor in resources. The population growth has a damaging effect on the flora and fauna.

In recent years, the allod has seen the increasing numbers of the Draconids who are likely to start competing for the remaining resources with the Orcs.

[Map missing]

The only allod where the orcs could feel more or less, as they say, "at home" was the allod of Izune, which survived thanks to the presence of the Great Dragoness Soliskar: being a magical creature, she held the allod back from being swallowed by the Astral by the very fact of her existence. Several orc tribes, feuding with one another, survived here. True, a mage soon arrived from Xadagan, and the dragoness had to leave Izune. It was here that Rodogor became Supreme Shaman.
